messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT created for #incidents — paging oncall for tenant latticepay (dedicated pool). symptom: streaming p99 spike + mid-response stalls. SLO p99 breached for that tenant. thread_ts=1767001234
Emily: I'm oncall — paging in. Alert shows p95 ~280ms, streaming p99 ~3.2s for latticepay-eu. Error rate creeping up to ~0.6%. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.team/reds/streams?c=latticepay
Raj: ack. I see GPU queue depth spikes and noticeable CPU steal on the eu-west serving nodes around 14:02 UTC. Lots of long-prefix requests surfaced in logs. KV cache churn looks high.
Sasha: is the impact global or constrained to their dedicated eu pool? customer is supposed to route primarily to eu-west-1.
Maria: confirmed — only the eu-west-1 dedicated pool for latticepay is flapping. us-east fallback shows normal p99. eu cluster has many inflight sessions from same tenant id.
Emily: customer note: they saw streaming stalls mid-response and sometimes resume after 2-5s. They mentioned a batch job kicked off ~13:58 that faned out many long-context prompts.
Kevin: quick log snippet:
```\nkubectl -n dedicated-latticepay logs -l app=runtime --since=10m | grep \"KV_CACHE\"\n... 2026-02-12T14:02:11Z INFO KV_CACHE_MISS prefix_len=20480 tenant=latticepay session=abc123\n... 2026-02-12T14:02:12Z WARN KV_CACHE_EVICT rate=high tenant=latticepay\n```
Kevin: TL;DR — prefixes ~20k tokens creating large KV entries, evictions spike and rebuilds serialize, causing tail latency.
Raj: runtime telemetry shows per-token cost increases ~6x on a cold KV rebuild for those long prefixes. Batching can't hide the serialized rebuilds.
Emily: quick impact calc: ~120 active sessions, ~30% of in-flight streaming requests experienced stalls — primarily affecting tenant p99. Platform-wide hosted SLOs intact but Dedicated SLA risk.
Sasha: any recent pool config/rollout changes? autoscaler tweaks?
Maria: checked the console — no config rollouts in past 24h. Autoscaler did scale but pods couldn't warm KV before traffic hit; CPU spike blocked recovery.
Kevin: mitigation options (ranked least invasive -> heavier):
- route new requests for latticepay to us-east fallback pool (region failover)
- reduce max_concurrency on eu-west latticepay pool to blunt incoming bursts
- enable experimental prefix-trim heuristic to cap prefix length (quality tradeoff)
- increase KV cache capacity (node resize + rollout)

Emily: let's do non-invasive first: 1) enable region failover to us-east for new sessions, 2) lower concurrency cap on eu-west pool. If p99 doesn't drop to acceptable levels, pursue cache increase.
Raj: applying routing change now — setting tenant failover to us-east.
Deploy Bot: routing-policy-update started — policy_id=rp-8873
Deploy Bot: routing-policy-update success — policy_id=rp-8873 applied; new traffic for tenant latticepay will prefer us-east fallback.
Emily: lowering eu-west pool max_concurrency from 64 -> 16 for latticepay to limit burst. Applying via console.
Ops Bot: concurrency-limit update initiated for pool dedicated-latticepay-eu: max_concurrency=16
Ops Bot: concurrency-limit update complete
Maria: metrics update — within 90s p95 improved 280ms -> 220ms, p99 streaming dropped 3.2s -> 1.1s for eu-west. Error rate fell to ~0.15%.
Kevin: good signs. us-east is taking new sessions; watch egress costs and international latency for customer.
Raj: residual stalls visible for sessions that hit cold KV rebuilds — those complete but still contribute to tail. Expect stabilization over next few minutes.
Emily: customer comms: @latticepay-support we've applied temporary throttles and region failover. Please pause any large fanout/batch jobs for ~20 minutes while we stabilize. Who can reach out?
Kevin: messaged their tech slack: "We observed a large fanout from your account causing tail stalls. We've throttled and routed new traffic to a fallback region. Please pause batch jobs for 20m while we stabilize."
Customer Bot: LatticePay acknowledged; they'll pause in ~5m.
Sasha: FYI — prefix-trim is available as a flip but degrades output completeness. Recommend only if p99 stays >1s after 10m.
Raj: agreed. We'll hold trim as last-resort. Also prepping node resize play: spin a temporary larger-memory nodepool to increase KV capacity and migrate traffic if needed.
Infra Bot: resize request submitted — ticket INF-9921
Kevin: collecting RCA artifacts: peak concurrent sessions, prefix length histogram, per-tenant KV hit/miss rates, autoscaler scale events, kernel CPU steal traces, and any recent rollout metadata.
Raj: saving ktrace and logs to incident folder: /incidents/1767001234-latticepay-kvcache
Emily: STATUS (14:18 UTC): mitigations active, p99 trending down, customer paused job. Next steps: 1) continue monitoring until stable, 2) follow-up RCA and tenant-specific KV cache tuning, 3) consider hard prefix limits or per-tenant QoS to protect pool.
Kevin: action items assigned: infra to evaluate cache-capacity increase (INF-9921), runtime team to consider a safe prefix-trim threshold and guardrails, oncall to monitor p99 for 30m, comms team to draft post-incident email for latticepay.
Emily: I'll keep the channel updated. If p99 resurges, we'll flip to plan B (prefix-trim) and escalate.
